# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 65 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 48 | Coptic

---

## Saying 65

**1** He said: "A creditable man owned a vineyard. He gave it on lease to tenant farmers so that they would cultivate it and he would receive its fruit from them. He sent his servant so that the farmers might give him the fruit of the vineyard. They seized his servant, beat him, and nearly killed him. The servant returned and told his master. His master said: 'Perhaps they did not recognize him.' He sent another servant. The farmers beat that one too. Then the master sent his son and said: 'Perhaps they will show some respect for my son.' Since the farmers knew that he was the heir of the vineyard, they seized him and killed him. Let him who has ears hear."

---

**Translator's Notes (LOGOS):**

- "Creditable man" for *agathos* — "good" in the moral sense; "creditable" suggests social standing also
- "Cultivate" rather than "work" — agricultural precision
- "Recognize him" — the master's naivety framed as a recognition problem
